title: Influence of DNA Sequences on the Thermodynamic and Structural Stability of the ZTA Transcription Factor horizontal line DNA Complex: An All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Study.
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过全原子分子动力学和增强采样模拟，系统探究EBV转录因子ZTA与不同DNA序列（核心基序及侧翼序列）复合物的热力学稳定性、结合亲和力及互作机制，精准聚焦TF-DNA结合体系并采用物理模拟方法，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is one of the cancer-causing gamma-type viruses. Although more than 90% of people are infected by this virus at some point, it remains in the body in a latent state, typically causing only minor symptoms. Our current understanding is that a known transcription factor (TF), the ZTA protein, binds with dsDNA (double-stranded DNA) and plays a crucial role in mediating the viral latent-to-lytic cycle through binding of specific ZTA-responsive elements (ZREs). However, there is no clear understanding of the effect of DNA sequences on the structural stability and quantitative estimation of the binding affinity between ZTA TF and DNA, along with their mechanistic details. In this study, we employed classical all-atom molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling simulations to study the ZTA-dsDNA structural properties, thermodynamics, and mechanistic details for the ZTA protein and for two different dsDNA systems: the core motif and the core motif with flanking end sequences. We conducted residue-level and nucleic acid-level analyses to assess the important protein residues and DNA bases forming interactions between the ZTA and dsDNA systems. We also explored the effect of adding flanking end sequences to the core motif on DNA groove lengths and interstrand hydrogen bonds. Our results indicate that the flanking sequences surrounding the core motif significantly influence the structural stability and binding affinity of the ZTA-dsDNA complex. Among ZRE 1, ZRE 2, and ZRE 3, particularly when paired with their naturally occurring flanking ends, ZRE 3 exhibits higher stability and binding affinity. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying EBV pathogenesis and may indicate potential targets for therapeutic intervention. A detailed explanation of the binding mechanisms will allow for the design of better-targeted therapies against EBV-associated cancers. This study will serve as a holistic benchmark for future studies of these viral protein interactions.
abstract_zh: EB病毒（Epstein-Barr virus, EBV）是一种致癌的γ型病毒。尽管超过90%的人群在某个阶段感染过该病毒，但它以潜伏状态存留于体内，通常仅引起轻微症状。目前的理解是，一种已知的转录因子（transcription factor, TF），即ZTA蛋白，与双链DNA（double-stranded DNA, dsDNA）结合，并通过特异性结合ZTA响应元件（ZTA-responsive elements, ZREs）在介导病毒从潜伏期到裂解期的转换中发挥关键作用。然而，关于DNA序列对ZTA转录因子与DNA之间结构稳定性及结合亲和力定量估计的影响，以及其机制细节，目前尚不明确。在本研究中，我们采用经典的全原子分子动力学（molecular dynamics）和增强采样模拟，研究了ZTA蛋白与两种不同dsDNA系统（核心基序及带有侧翼末端序列的核心基序）的结构特性、热力学性质及机制细节。我们进行了残基水平和核酸水平分析，以评估ZTA与dsDNA系统间形成相互作用的重要蛋白残基和DNA碱基。我们还探讨了在核心基序中添加侧翼末端序列对DNA沟长度和链间氢键的影响。结果表明，核心基序周围的侧翼序列显著影响ZTA-dsDNA复合物的结构稳定性和结合亲和力。在ZRE 1、ZRE 2和ZRE 3中，特别是当与其天然侧翼末端配对时，ZRE 3表现出更高的稳定性和结合亲和力。这些发现为EBV发病机制的分子机制提供了见解，并可能指示治疗干预的潜在靶点。对结合机制的详细解释将有助于设计针对EBV相关癌症的更精准疗法。本研究将为未来这些病毒蛋白相互作用的研究提供一个整体基准。
